## What is our view?

We have no model of our own for this market, so the odds above are the traders' consensus and not an independent estimate. For calibration: in our sample of settled Elections markets, the Kalshi mid-price a day before close scored a Brier error of 0.0021 (a coin-flip price scores 0.25; lower is better).

## How does this market resolve?

> If at least 116,000,000 valid, blank and null votes, in combination are cast in the first round of the 2026 Brazilian presidential election, then the market resolves to Yes.

Close: October 4, 2026 at 03:59 UTC. Expected settlement: October 11, 2026 at 14:00 UTC. Settlement source: [Tribunal Superior Eleitoral](https://www.tse.jus.br/). Full terms: [Kalshi contract terms](https://assets.kalshi.com/contract_terms/VOTECOUNT.pdf).

## What could move the odds?

- New polls, official results as they are reported, and certification timelines.
- A rules clarification or settlement-source change published by Kalshi on the market page.
- Order-book depth: thin books move on small orders, so a large price move on little volume says little.

## How reliable are markets like this one?

Across 3 settled Elections markets in our sample (Kalshi, 2026-09-29 to 2026-10-03), the Kalshi mid-price about 24 hours before close had a Brier error of 0.0021; a coin-flip price scores 0.25 and lower is better. Contracts quoted at 5 cents or less settled YES 0% of the time (2 markets); contracts quoted at 95 cents or more settled YES 100.0% (1 markets). The sample covers a few weeks, so it is a guide to how markets like this have behaved, not a guarantee of how this one will settle.

object.primary: If at least 116,000,000 valid, blank and null votes, in combination are cast in the first round of the 2026 Brazilian presidential election, then the market resolves to Yes.
object.secondary:
The count is the total of voters who voted (comparecimento) in the presidential contest of the first round of Brazil’s 2026 general election, as reported by the Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE), including those who cast blank or null votes. Registered voters, abstentions, justified absences and ballots in other contests do not count.

Subject to the contract’s Fully-Conducted Elections and Accelerated Resolution Upon Designated Media Source Declarations provisions, the vote count refers to the officially certified results from the relevant election authority. Provisional, absentee, early, mail-in, or electronic ballots are included only if reflected in the official certification.

The contract resolves based on officially certified results regardless of ongoing appeals. Outside those two contract provisions, preliminary counts, exit polls, projections, or uncertified results do not qualify.
